text:
maria chen: Quick signal — after the proxy change I'm seeing a bunch of ~10-20ms traces that have no meaningful spans and they're blowing up cost attribution queries. Anyone else notice an entropy spike?
ajay singh: saw it this morning. sampler vs pre-enrich boundary seems misaligned. Many tiny envelopes get expanded during enrichment and duplicate tenant keys.
lee park: can you paste one of the raw envelopes?
maria chen: ```json
{"trace_id":"abc123","spans":[{"id":"1","name":"proxy.recv","dur_ms":5},{"id":"2","name":"proxy.fanout","dur_ms":8}],"attrs":{"tenant_id":"t-42","service":"edge-proxy"}}
```
carol nielsen: ugh, the fanout span is being emitted per backend response; aggregation happens later in the pipeline. that multiplies cost and cardinality.
ajay singh: tradeoff: dedupe at gateway (cheap, avoids churn) vs do late-merge in ingest (keeps gateway simple but increases downstream load).
lee park: dedupe at gateway is tempting but dangerous for compliance customers who rely on unaltered envelopes. also we'd be losing raw telemetry for some debug flows.
maria chen: true — maybe we can add an opt-in gateway flag to compact fanout for non-compliance tenants?
carol nielsen: we also need to consider attribution. Currently billing keys get set during enrichment; if we dedupe earlier we must preserve enough lineage to reconstruct billing.
ajay singh: proposed hybrid: compact at gateway to a compact envelope with an ancestry array: `ancestry: [span_ids]` and keep `original_count` metadata. ingest then expands only for debug queries. default path keeps compact representation for metrics and cost pipelines.
lee park: that sounds workable. impacts: change in schema (new `ancestry`), enrichment codepath must tolerate compact envelopes, and canonicalization logic must dedupe on ancestry rather than span id.
maria chen: approximate rollout plan: 1) RFC for compact-envelope schema and ancestry field (owner: ajay) 2) Gateway feature flag + opt-in for some tenants (owner: lee) 3) Ingest gateway importer handles compact envelopes (owner: carol) 4) Canary in prod on non-compliance tenants for 2 weeks, monitor cost delta and query shape (owner: maria)
carol nielsen: test concerns — need to update sampling sim harness. compacting changes sample rate math; we should run offline sim with last 7d of traffic. I can take that.
ajay singh: also need to update rollback plan: if queries that rely on raw spans fail, we should be able to toggle gateway to pass-through within 1 minute. add circuit-breaker to flag.
lee park: quick question: do we need any auth/permission checks for changing envelope content? compliance customers might require an audit log.
maria chen: yes — add a header `X-Compact-Enabled: true` and log per-tenant audit event. keep logs for 90d.
sre-bot: Incident note: deploy canary will trigger observability alert set `obs:canary-impact` if cost increases >15% vs baseline for 10m.
carol nielsen: action items summarized: Ajay write RFC + schema draft by EOD Wednesday; Lee implement gateway flag PoC; Maria run cost baseline and prepare canary dashboard; Carol run sim with 7d replay and update sampling sims. I'll create tickets.
ajay singh: one more: need to coordinate with billing team about `original_count` semantics — they will want deterministic mapping for chargeback. I'll ping them in the RFC.
maria chen: cool — thanks everyone. if we hit edge cases we can fallback to late-merge path. otherwise this should cut ingest cardinality and cost while keeping debuggability. :thumbsup:
lee park: +1. I'll start the flag impl and drop a short PR link when I have initial tests.
carol nielsen: logging note: ensure that compacting doesn't strip `request_id` or any PII-critical fields; otherwise support flows break.
maria chen: noted. leaving the thread here but will post RFC link once ajay has it.
